name: The Bodrum EDITION
insider_take: Perched on the pristine shores of Yalikavak Bay, this sleek sanctuary marries Ian Schrager's legendary design prowess with Turkey's captivating Aegean coastline – where ancient Halicarnassus meets contemporary luxury.
whats_special: The hotel sits in Yalikavak, home to the ultra-luxe Palmarina – one of Europe's most exclusive superyacht marinas. The property features stunning infinity pools that seem to blend seamlessly with the turquoise Aegean Sea, while the nearby ancient city of Halicarnassus (modern Bodrum) was once home to one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World – the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus.
pro_tip: Book a sunset dinner at the hotel's waterfront restaurant during the "meltem" season (June-September) when the cool northern winds create perfect sailing conditions and dramatic evening skies.
dont_miss: A private boat trip to explore the hidden coves of the Bodrum Peninsula, or venture to nearby Rabbit Island for snorkeling in crystal-clear waters. The charming fishing village of Gumusluk, just 15 minutes away, offers authentic Turkish dining with tables literally on the beach where you can walk to nearby Rabbit Island during low tide.
pros: Stunning Mediterranean beachfront location with pristine private beach access
Exceptional contemporary design blending modern luxury with Turkish Riviera charm
World-class spa and wellness facilities with authentic Turkish treatments
Outstanding culinary experiences featuring Mediterranean and international cuisine
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive positioning
Sophisticated adult-oriented atmosphere may not suit families with young children
